source: Solar constant: NASA NSSDCA Sun fact sheet. Margins: NASA mass and power margin practice at preliminary design (GSFC-STD-1000 Gold Rules, about 20-30%). Link reference: Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (100 W X-band, 3 m antenna, about 0.5 Mbps to a 34 m Deep Space Network antenna at 2.67 au; NASA MRO telecommunications fact sheet), scaled to 1 W, 1 m and 1 au. Schedule risk by technology readiness level and the redundancy and tier factors are game balance values.
units: Margins and fractions are 0-1. link_reference gives the downlink rate of a 1 W transmitter with a 1 m antenna at 1 au into a 34 m ground antenna. schedule_slip_warning and mission_loss_risk_warning are the probabilities above which the schedule and risk lines turn to a warning. delta_v_margin.target is the propellant reserve loaded on top of the planned manoeuvres. simulation: battery_reserve_fraction is the charge at which a shadow sortie is abandoned, recharge_fraction the charge needed to start one, shadow_transit_fraction the share of a sortie spent driving in and out, ice_find_by_depth the chance factor of reaching ice with a drill of that depth, scripted_pilot the inputs the fast simulation uses in place of a human (operations_efficiency 1 is a skilled crew). scoring: points for full science, for an unspent budget (scaled by the margin), for launching with every budget healthy, for surviving to the end and for co-op coordination; threshold_credit is the share of an objective earned at its threshold; returned_data_weight is how much of the science depends on the data actually reaching Earth; the two science fractions grade the outcome. coordination_response_seconds is how fast a role must answer its event to count toward the coordination points. autonomous_planning_factor multiplies the planning time between shadow sorties for a computer with autonomy level 2.
